variants.headline: A friend in the {{era}}: {{civilization}}
body: Word from {{civilization}} says the {{former}} is behind it and the {{era}} has begun. Its envoy in our capital spent the morning answering the same question from every merchant: what will the new workshops sell, and when? Our guilds should send a buyer before the first crates are spoken for.

variants.headline: A friend crosses into the {{era}}
body: Letters from a friendly court inform us that {{civilization}} has passed out of the {{former}} and into the {{era}}, and that its scholars are already borrowing books they once thought beyond them. We are told the first public lecture drew a crowd that filled the hall and part of the street. A neighbor who learns in the open like that is a neighbor worth keeping.

variants.headline: A new age in {{civilization}}, they say
body: They say a boy brought home a counting board marked in a way his father could not read. Traders said {{civilization}} had entered the {{era}} and its clerks now reckoned faster than ours. The father kept the board on the shelf and told the boy to learn the markings before the traders changed their minds.

variants.headline: Of {{civilization}}'s entry into the {{era}}
body: In this season {{civilization}} set aside the {{former}} and took up the {{era}}, and its nearest city stands {{distance}} from our own according to the rolls. The warden of the boundary road was asked to count the wagons passing in a week and found more than he expected. He entered the number without comment, as the custom is.

variants.headline: What a friend's new era means
body: The {{era}} has reached our friend's workshops, and the {{former}} is now a thing its apprentices study from old drawings. The ceremony matters less than what follows it: our professors have begun asking for places at its schools, and its scholars have begun asking for ours. A friendship that trades students as well as goods will outlast any treaty signed in a hall.

variants.headline: New learning on the frontier: {{tech}}
body: {{team}} has learned {{tech}}, and its cities stand close enough that our own smiths hear of every change within a week. At the frontier market a cooper asked a passing carter what the news would mean for barrels, and got a shrug for an answer. Our guilds should expect the question from their own customers soon.

variants.headline: New knowledge in {{team}}: {{tech}}
body: {{team}} now hold {{tech}} between them, and each court has sent word that the rest had nothing to do with it. The clerks name the same scholars in different orders, which is how a shared discovery is made to look like several. What reaches us is the knowledge itself, and it now sits on both sides of a border we share.

variants.headline: A neighbor's new learning
body: What does {{tech}} in the hands of {{team}} change for us? Their workshops keep lamps burning past midnight now, and a drover who passes the gate says the guards have stopped asking his business. A neighbor with new tools and late hours is preparing for something, and our own benches should not be the last to hear of it.

variants.headline: Notice to the learned: {{tech}} abroad
body: The printers give notice that {{tech}} is now in use in {{team}}, whose lands lie near ours. Scholars who can show the report to be mistaken should call at the office before the next edition. Until then the notice stands.

variants.headline: New learning across the fence
body: The quarrel began over a loaf and ended with half the street choosing sides: {{tech}} has reached {{team}}, and no one could agree whether it would make bread cheaper or just make bakers quicker. The old miller ended it by thumping the counter. "Cheaper or dearer," he said, "they will still want it buttered."

variants.headline: The lamp next door
body: {{tech}} lights the neighbor's table. Trim your own wick before dark.

variants.headline: Our nation enters the {{era}}
body: Our nation is in the {{era}} now, and the change shows first in small rooms rather than great halls. At the land office, a clerk has been copying the same map for years, and this week he was told the old sheet will no longer do. He has not thrown it away.

variants.headline: Hear it! The {{era}} is ours
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! The {{era}} has come, and no town meets it alone. Light a lamp in the window tonight, and let the next street see it and light another.

variants.headline: The {{era}} begins tonight
body: Tonight the country is in the {{era}}. In workshops and kitchens, people are trying out words that were strange last month. A girl in the capital asked her father what he would make first, and he said he did not know yet. The whole age is waiting for his answer.

variants.headline: The record of our passage into the {{era}}
body: In this year the nation entered the {{era}}, and the bells were rung at every shrine before the proclamation was read. The keeper of the chief shrine gave thanks for the scholars who labored unseen and asked the congregation to remember them in prayer. The scribes set down the date twice, so that no later hand might shorten it.

variants.headline: The bells rang all morning
body: Madam Editor, the clerks have worked toward the {{era}} for years, and this week the city finally noticed. My office has not had a quiet hour since the proclamation, because every neighbor now wants a form filled out for something new. The government promised this age and delivered it; a word of thanks would not be wasted on the men who keep the ledgers.

variants.headline: The scholars finish {{tech}}
body: The scholars have finished {{tech}}, and the {{terms.civic.government}} had the first written account on its table before noon. A second copy went to the printer, and a third has gone missing between the lecture hall and the archive. The archivist has pinned a note to the door, though she has not named the borrower.

variants.headline: Who can teach {{tech}} next?
body: The real test of {{tech}} begins after the cheering stops: can anyone teach it? One of the demonstrators has spent the week writing out the steps for a colleague in a town that missed the trials, in words a first-year pupil could follow. A method that lives in one head dies with it; a method written down belongs to the nation.

variants.headline: One more for the home team
body: {{tech}} is ours. The scholars get the credit, the printers get the work, and the rest of us get one more useful thing by next season.

variants.headline: Notice: {{tech}} is finished
body: Notice is given that our scholars have brought {{tech}} to its end. One copy goes to the archive before any is sold. Let the {{era}} count it among its works, and let the hands that made it be named.

variants.headline: At the market, the word is {{tech}}
body: The news beat the mayor's clerk to the market: {{tech}} is ours, someone shouted, and for an hour nobody knew whether that meant cheaper salt. A porter asked what good it would do a man with no workshop, and the crowd laughed. The clerk arrived to find his announcement already old.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} crosses into the {{era}}
body: {{civilization}} has put the {{former}} behind it and entered the {{era}}, and the first sign here was a price list. A cloth merchant found that her agent there had raised his rates before the proclamation was even dry. She has kept the old list pinned above the new one, she says, to remind herself what caution costs.

variants.headline: A rival leaves the {{former}}
body: We are advised from abroad that {{civilization}}, whose friendship we do not claim, has quitted the {{former}} for the {{era}}. A professor here has already ordered its new treatises for the university shelf, saying a rival's book is cheaper than a rival's mistake. Whether the crossing deserves our envy or our attention, the reader may judge.

variants.headline: Up the road, a new era
body: {{civilization}} is in the {{era}} as of this week, and its nearest city is only {{distance}} from our own gate. No army has crossed. No stone has moved. The neighbor simply knows more than it did last month, and that is usually how trouble begins.

variants.headline: It is told of {{civilization}}
body: It is told that when the {{era}} reached {{civilization}}, the grandmothers hid the old seed jars in the rafters and would not say where. The young ones laughed and bought new ones. The jars are still up there, and the tellers say nobody has needed them yet.

variants.headline: A rival enters the {{era}}. And us?
body: {{civilization}} has entered the {{era}}, {{terms.civic.people}}, and its {{player.civic.government}} will soon be telling anyone who listens how little it cost. Ask our own {{terms.civic.government}} the same question and watch the answer turn into a speech. What did we pay to keep pace, and whose purse was opened? A government that cannot show the bill should not ask for the credit.

variants.headline: First in learning: {{civilization}}
body: {{civilization}} now stands first in learning, with {{count|known technology|known technologies}} to its name. A bookseller here has cleared a shelf for the leading country's newest journals and put a card in the window before a single volume arrived. First place is a loan, not a gift, and the shelf remembers who earned it.

variants.headline: A new nation stands first in learning
body: A nation we cannot name has taken the lead in learning with {{count|known technology|known technologies}}, and the dispatch that brought the count left the name to rumor. The reading room has had a request for a journal nobody can order. The librarian has put a blank card in the catalogue and told her assistant to fill it in when the world says who.

variants.headline: The learning count, restated
body: At the top of the learning tally: {{civilization}}
Works counted: {{count}}
Rivals ahead: none

variants.headline: First place, shared
body: {{civilization}} leads the world with {{count|art or science|arts and sciences}}. Someone else has the same number. The top step was not built for a crowd.

variants.headline: Two ways to count learning
body: The nation at the top of the tally can claim {{count|art or science|arts and sciences}}, but a count of works says little about a school. Walk into one old academy and you will find the lecture hall crowded for a subject the tally barely notices, while the room for a celebrated art stands empty. A rival further down may be filling more benches in the arts we share, and the ledger will never show it.
